content_html:
Stops destructive SQL before it reaches your database, whether it comes from AI agents, scripts or people, with no code changes.

AI agents, scripts and people all run SQL against production with real credentials. Nobody reads each statement before it runs, and a database role decides what a user may touch, not whether this particular statement should run. One DELETE without a WHERE empties a table. A SELECT of the wrong columns copies emails or card numbers to wherever the result goes.

vericto-proxy sits between your clients and the database, on the database's own wire protocol. It parses every query with the vericto-engine AST parser, checks it against your rules, and either forwards it to the real database or blocks it with a normal SQL error. Your application only changes the host and port in its connection string.

License. Source-available under the FSL-1.1-ALv2. You can self-host it and use it for free, including in production at a for-profit company. What it does not allow is a Competing Use: making it available to others in a commercial product or service that substitutes for it or offers substantially similar functionality, such as a SQL firewall service built on it. Each release also becomes Apache-2.0 two years after Vericto makes it available. LICENSING.md answers the common questions.

One proxy instance fronts one database and speaks exactly one wire protocol, chosen at deploy time with VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL:

VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL Databases Block response
postgres (default) PostgreSQL native ErrorResponse SQLSTATE 42501
mysql MySQL native ERR_Packet ERROR 1142

Everything else — configuration, evaluation, telemetry — is the same across engines. Only the value above and (optionally) the default ports change.

No AI, no stochastic heuristics — the same input always produces the same result.

Other dialects (Oracle, SQL Server, Snowflake, SQLite): evaluate via the HTTP API, the CLI or MCP; there is no wire proxy for them. Snowflake has no TCP wire protocol at all, so VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL=snowflake stops the proxy at startup with an error. SQLite is a library linked into the application, with no wire protocol either: its SQL is checked in the application, before it runs.

Try it with Docker

All you need is Docker: no account, no API key, no build. This starts a throwaway Postgres, puts the proxy in front of it with the built-in ruleset, and sends a few queries through it with the psql that ships in the Postgres image. The password demo is only for this disposable database.

docker network create vericto-demo
docker run -d --name vericto-demo-db --network vericto-demo \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=demo postgres:17
docker run -d --name vericto-demo-proxy --network vericto-demo \
  -e UPSTREAM_HOST=vericto-demo-db vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0
until docker exec vericto-demo-db pg_isready -q -h localhost -U postgres; do sleep 1; done

docker run --rm --network vericto-demo postgres:17 \
  psql postgresql://postgres:demo@vericto-demo-proxy:5433/postgres \
  -c "CREATE TABLE users (id int PRIMARY KEY, email text)" \
  -c "INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'ana@example.com'), (42, 'bo@example.com')" \
  -c "DELETE FROM users" \
  -c "DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 42" \
  -c "SELECT id, email FROM users"

The image comes from Docker Hub; ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0 serves the same digest (see Docker).

The DELETE without a WHERE never reaches the database; the one with a WHERE does:

CREATE TABLE
INSERT 0 2
ERROR:  Vericto blocked this query [VERICTO-001] — AST node: DeleteStmt > WhereClause = NULL. Suggestion: DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1
DELETE 1
 id |      email
----+-----------------
  1 | ana@example.com
(1 row)

docker logs vericto-demo-proxy shows the decision. To put the proxy in front of your own database, see Docker and Connection strings. Clean up with:

docker rm -f vericto-demo-db vericto-demo-proxy && docker network rm vericto-demo

Architecture position

Your app / ORM
     │
     │  SQL wire protocol (proxy listen port, default 5433)
     ▼
 vericto-proxy   ──── vericto-engine (lib) ────►  ALLOWED / BLOCKED
     │
     │  (if ALLOWED) forwards query
     ▼
 Real database upstream

Point your DATABASE_URL host at vericto-proxy instead of your real database. No code changes required — your ORM/driver is unaware of the proxy.

What it blocks

With the built-in ruleset, these never reach the database:

  • DELETE / UPDATE without WHERE
  • DROP TABLE, DROP SCHEMA, TRUNCATE
  • OR-tautology SQL injection (WHERE id = $1 OR 1=1)
  • ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN / RENAME
  • … full rule list →

Lower-severity findings — SELECT * without WHERE, SELECT without LIMIT, INSERT without an explicit column list — are forwarded and recorded rather than blocked. With the control-plane link on, the workspace policy decides the action for each severity.

Bounded reads (4.17.0). To cap what an agent reads instead of only flagging it, a business policy with action: { rewrite_limit: n } (the LIMIT cap template in rewrite mode) makes the proxy forward the statement with LIMIT n added, or a larger LIMIT lowered, on Postgres and MySQL, simple and prepared statements. It needs VERICTO_POLICY_RULES=enforce; see docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

A blocked query is returned as a native error for the active protocol (see the table above), so no special handling is needed in your application.

Sensitive columns

Columns can be tagged as sensitive per database in the Vericto dashboard (Team and Enterprise plans). The tags reach the proxy with the ruleset (/sync/rules, so the control-plane link and VERICTO_DATABASE_ID are required) and are enforced on the wire, before the database sees the query. When a query reads several tagged columns the strictest policy wins (block > mask > flag). The proxy enforces: unlike the Validation API or the CLI, which only advise, what the proxy decides is what the database receives.

Policy Postgres MySQL
block The query never reaches the database: ErrorResponse, SQLSTATE 42501 Never reaches the database: ERR_Packet, ERROR 1142
flag Forwarded as sent, recorded as FLAGGED Same
mask The proxy forwards a rewritten query in which the column is masked (full, last4, email or hash) under its own name, and never the original. The client receives masked values. Same: the proxy forwards the rewritten query in the same COM_QUERY or COM_STMT_PREPARE, and never the original.

If a rewrite does not hold together, the proxy blocks with VERICTO-085 rather than forward the original. SELECT * over a table with a masked or blocked column is blocked; list the columns. The full behaviour (both protocols, prepared statements, fail-safe cases, parse errors, telemetry, known limits) is in docs/SENSITIVE_COLUMNS.md.

Agent access

An allowlist per database user (Team and Enterprise plans), set in the Vericto dashboard: which tables and columns that user may read, and which it may write. Everything else is denied (VERICTO-087). The policies reach the proxy with the ruleset (/sync/rules, so the control-plane link and VERICTO_DATABASE_ID are required), keyed by database user, with an optional "*" default for every user not listed.

The identity of a session is the database user it authenticated as, so give each agent its own database user and a policy for that user. Under a policy, every reference counts (WHERE, JOIN, subqueries, RETURNING, not only what the query returns), DDL is always denied, and the identity cannot be changed from inside the session (SET ROLE, USE, COM_CHANGE_USER and the like are denied). A policy in observe mode records what it would deny and forwards the query.

The full behaviour (name resolution, writes and locks, policy changes on open sessions, telemetry, known limits) is in docs/AGENT_ACCESS.md.

Configuration

All variables are dialect-agnostic — the same names apply to every engine.

Required

Variable Description
UPSTREAM_HOST Hostname of the real database to proxy to

Ports

Variable Default Description
UPSTREAM_PORT protocol default¹ Port of the upstream database
PROXY_LISTEN_PORT protocol default¹ Port the proxy listens on

¹ Defaults follow VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL: Postgres 5432 upstream / 5433 listen; MySQL 3306 upstream / 3307 listen.

Everything else

The rest is optional and documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md:

  • Control-plane link (VERICTO_API_URL, VERICTO_API_KEY, VERICTO_DATABASE_ID, all three together): reports decisions to the Vericto API and syncs the workspace's rules and policy. Without it the proxy still protects with the built-in ruleset, and reports nothing. Also covers the telemetry buffer, over the monthly quota, disk spool size and several proxies on one volume.
  • TLS on each hop, client→proxy and proxy→database. On MySQL, TLS must be on both hops or neither.
  • Query size limit (VERICTO_MAX_QUERY_BYTES, 10 MiB by default).
  • Business policy rules (VERICTO_POLICY_RULES, off by default): a preview, off unless you turn it on; with it off the proxy behaves exactly as 4.14.3. With it on, the proxy applies only sync bundles whose Ed25519 signature verifies (VERICTO_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEYS for a control plane other than Vericto's).
  • Health check for load balancers (VERICTO_HEALTHZ_PORT).
  • Observability: logs, and metrics as Prometheus or CloudWatch EMF.
  • CPU sizing: capacity per vCPU, when to scale out (CPU at 50–60% of the task's reservation), and VERICTO_WORKER_THREADS (by default sized from the container's CPU limit, 1 worker on a 0.5 vCPU task).
  • Engine-specific notes, including MySQL details (TLS, protocol compression).

To run from source and run the tests, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

Docker

Release images are published on Docker Hub as vericto/vericto-proxy (from 4.14.1 on) and at ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, and pull without credentials. The release workflow copies the multi-arch index it pushed to GHCR, so both registries serve the same digest under the same tags (<version>, <major>.<minor>, <major> and latest): pull from whichever your environment allows.

# Postgres. On Linux, add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway
docker run --rm -e UPSTREAM_HOST=host.docker.internal -p 5433:5433 \
  vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0

# MySQL
docker run --rm \
  -e VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL=mysql \
  -e UPSTREAM_HOST=host.docker.internal \
  -p 3307:3307 \
  vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0

# The same image from GHCR
docker pull ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0

Images released from now on carry a build provenance attestation (Sigstore, GitHub Actions) that ties their digest to this repository, the release workflow and the commit. Verify one before you deploy it, and deploy by digest:

gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:<version> --repo vericto/vericto-proxy

# Docker Hub (4.14.1 and later): the same digest, attested under its Docker Hub name
gh attestation verify oci://docker.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:<version> --repo vericto/vericto-proxy

Each platform image (4.15.2 and later) also carries a signed SPDX SBOM attestation, made for the platform manifest's digest (docker buildx imagetools inspect lists both):

gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy@<platform digest> \
  --repo vericto/vericto-proxy --predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3

The runtime base is Chainguard glibc-dynamic (4.15.2 and later; debian:bookworm-slim before): glibc, libgcc and the CA bundle, no shell and no package manager. The proxy runs as 65532:65532 (nonroot; it was 1001:1001 up to 4.15.1, so chown a volume an older image wrote, or pass --user 1001:1001). Health checks call the binary instead of a shell, in exec form: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/vericto-proxy", "healthcheck"] (Docker Compose healthcheck.test, ECS healthCheck.command). It connects to the healthz listener (VERICTO_HEALTHZ_PORT) and exits 0 when that succeeds or the port is not set, 1 otherwise. A CMD-SHELL check, bash -c, curl or wget fails in this image.

To build the image from this checkout instead:

docker build -t vericto/proxy:local .

With Docker Compose:

proxy:
  image: ${VERICTO_PROXY_IMAGE:-vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0}
  ports:
    - "5433:5433"
  environment:
    UPSTREAM_HOST: postgres
    UPSTREAM_PORT: "5432"
    PROXY_LISTEN_PORT: "5433"
    # For MySQL: VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL: "mysql" + the matching ports.
    # Optional — uncomment for telemetry + rule sync (all three together):
    # VERICTO_API_URL: "https://api.vericto.com"
    # VERICTO_API_KEY: "${VERICTO_API_KEY}"
    # VERICTO_DATABASE_ID: "${VERICTO_DATABASE_ID}"

Connection strings

Connection string
Postgres via proxy postgres://user:pass@localhost:5433/mydb
MySQL via proxy mysql://user:pass@localhost:3307/mydb

Same credentials as a direct connection — only the host/port change.

Contributing

Wire-protocol, TLS, telemetry and deployment fixes belong here; rules and parser changes belong in vericto-engine. See CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md.

Versions 4.13.0 and earlier remain under the Elastic License 2.0. LICENSING.md answers the common questions, including how the embedded vericto-engine is licensed; see also NOTICE and TRADEMARKS.md. For a commercial license contact enterprise@vericto.com.

The Docker image carries LICENSE, NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES (the licenses of every dependency compiled into the binary) in /usr/share/doc/vericto-proxy/, and the label org.opencontainers.image.licenses=FSL-1.1-ALv2:

id=$(docker create ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:latest)
docker cp "$id":/usr/share/doc/vericto-proxy/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES - | tar -xO
docker rm "$id" >/dev/null

Agent access

blocks.html_en: An allowlist per database user (Team and Enterprise plans), set in the Vericto dashboard: which tables and columns that user may read, and which it may write. Everything else is denied (VERICTO-087). The policies reach the proxy with the ruleset (/sync/rules, so the control-plane link and VERICTO_DATABASE_ID are required), keyed by database user, with an optional "*" default for every user not listed.

blocks.html_en: The identity of a session is the database user it authenticated as, so give each agent its own database user and a policy for that user. Under a policy, every reference counts (WHERE, JOIN, subqueries, RETURNING, not only what the query returns), DDL is always denied, and the identity cannot be changed from inside the session (SET ROLE, USE, COM_CHANGE_USER and the like are denied). A policy in observe mode records what it would deny and forwards the query.

blocks.html_en: The runtime base is Chainguard glibc-dynamic (4.15.2 and later; debian:bookworm-slim before): glibc, libgcc and the CA bundle, no shell and no package manager. The proxy runs as 65532:65532 (nonroot; it was 1001:1001 up to 4.15.1, so chown a volume an older image wrote, or pass --user 1001:1001). Health checks call the binary instead of a shell, in exec form: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/vericto-proxy", "healthcheck"] (Docker Compose healthcheck.test, ECS healthCheck.command). It connects to the healthz listener (VERICTO_HEALTHZ_PORT) and exits 0 when that succeeds or the port is not set, 1 otherwise. A CMD-SHELL check, bash -c, curl or wget fails in this image.

content_html_zh:
Stops destructive SQL before it reaches your database, whether it comes from AI agents, scripts or people, with no code changes.

AI agents, scripts and people all run SQL against production with real credentials. Nobody reads each statement before it runs, and a database role decides what a user may touch, not whether this particular statement should run. One DELETE without a WHERE empties a table. A SELECT of the wrong columns copies emails or card numbers to wherever the result goes.

vericto-proxy sits between your clients and the database, on the database's own wire protocol. It parses every query with the vericto-engine AST parser, checks it against your rules, and either forwards it to the real database or blocks it with a normal SQL error. Your application only changes the host and port in its connection string.

License. Source-available under the FSL-1.1-ALv2. You can self-host it and use it for free, including in production at a for-profit company. What it does not allow is a Competing Use: making it available to others in a commercial product or service that substitutes for it or offers substantially similar functionality, such as a SQL firewall service built on it. Each release also becomes Apache-2.0 two years after Vericto makes it available. LICENSING.md answers the common questions.

One proxy instance fronts one database and speaks exactly one wire protocol, chosen at deploy time with VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL:

VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL 数据库 Block response
postgres (default) PostgreSQL native ErrorResponse SQLSTATE 42501
mysql MySQL native ERR_Packet ERROR 1142

Everything else — configuration, evaluation, telemetry — is the same across engines. Only the value above and (optionally) the default ports change.

No AI, no stochastic heuristics — the same input always produces the same result.

Other dialects (Oracle, SQL Server, Snowflake, SQLite): evaluate via the HTTP API, the CLI or MCP; there is no wire proxy for them. Snowflake has no TCP wire protocol at all, so VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL=snowflake stops the proxy at startup with an error. SQLite is a library linked into the application, with no wire protocol either: its SQL is checked in the application, before it runs.

Try it with Docker

All you need is Docker: no account, no API key, no build. This starts a throwaway Postgres, puts the proxy in front of it with the built-in ruleset, and sends a few queries through it with the psql that ships in the Postgres image. The password demo is only for this disposable database.

docker network create vericto-demo
docker run -d --name vericto-demo-db --network vericto-demo \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=demo postgres:17
docker run -d --name vericto-demo-proxy --network vericto-demo \
  -e UPSTREAM_HOST=vericto-demo-db vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0
until docker exec vericto-demo-db pg_isready -q -h localhost -U postgres; do sleep 1; done

docker run --rm --network vericto-demo postgres:17 \
  psql postgresql://postgres:demo@vericto-demo-proxy:5433/postgres \
  -c "CREATE TABLE users (id int PRIMARY KEY, email text)" \
  -c "INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'ana@example.com'), (42, 'bo@example.com')" \
  -c "DELETE FROM users" \
  -c "DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 42" \
  -c "SELECT id, email FROM users"

The image comes from Docker Hub; ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0 serves the same digest (see Docker).

The DELETE without a WHERE never reaches the database; the one with a WHERE does:

CREATE TABLE
INSERT 0 2
ERROR:  Vericto blocked this query [VERICTO-001] — AST node: DeleteStmt > WhereClause = NULL. Suggestion: DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1
DELETE 1
 id |      email
----+-----------------
  1 | ana@example.com
(1 row)

docker logs vericto-demo-proxy shows the decision. To put the proxy in front of your own database, see Docker and Connection strings. Clean up with:

docker rm -f vericto-demo-db vericto-demo-proxy && docker network rm vericto-demo

Architecture position

Your app / ORM
     │
     │  SQL wire protocol (proxy listen port, default 5433)
     ▼
 vericto-proxy   ──── vericto-engine (lib) ────►  ALLOWED / BLOCKED
     │
     │  (if ALLOWED) forwards query
     ▼
 Real database upstream

Point your DATABASE_URL host at vericto-proxy instead of your real database. No code changes required — your ORM/driver is unaware of the proxy.

  • DELETE / UPDATE without WHERE
  • DROP TABLE, DROP SCHEMA, TRUNCATE
  • OR-tautology SQL injection (WHERE id = $1 OR 1=1)
  • ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN / RENAME
  • … full rule list →

Lower-severity findings — SELECT * without WHERE, SELECT without LIMIT, INSERT without an explicit column list — are forwarded and recorded rather than blocked. With the control-plane link on, the workspace policy decides the action for each severity.

Bounded reads (4.17.0). To cap what an agent reads instead of only flagging it, a business policy with action: { rewrite_limit: n } (the LIMIT cap template in rewrite mode) makes the proxy forward the statement with LIMIT n added, or a larger LIMIT lowered, on Postgres and MySQL, simple and prepared statements. It needs VERICTO_POLICY_RULES=enforce; see docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

A blocked query is returned as a native error for the active protocol (see the table above), so no special handling is needed in your application.

Sensitive columns

Columns can be tagged as sensitive per database in the Vericto dashboard (Team and Enterprise plans). The tags reach the proxy with the ruleset (/sync/rules, so the control-plane link and VERICTO_DATABASE_ID are required) and are enforced on the wire, before the database sees the query. When a query reads several tagged columns the strictest policy wins (block > mask > flag). The proxy enforces: unlike the Validation API or the CLI, which only advise, what the proxy decides is what the database receives.

block The query never reaches the database: ErrorResponse, SQLSTATE 42501 Never reaches the database: ERR_Packet, ERROR 1142
flag Forwarded as sent, recorded as FLAGGED Same
mask The proxy forwards a rewritten query in which the column is masked (full, last4, email or hash) under its own name, and never the original. The client receives masked values. Same: the proxy forwards the rewritten query in the same COM_QUERY or COM_STMT_PREPARE, and never the original.

If a rewrite does not hold together, the proxy blocks with VERICTO-085 rather than forward the original. SELECT * over a table with a masked or blocked column is blocked; list the columns. The full behaviour (both protocols, prepared statements, fail-safe cases, parse errors, telemetry, known limits) is in docs/SENSITIVE_COLUMNS.md.

Agent access

An allowlist per database user (Team and Enterprise plans), set in the Vericto dashboard: which tables and columns that user may read, and which it may write. Everything else is denied (VERICTO-087). The policies reach the proxy with the ruleset (/sync/rules, so the control-plane link and VERICTO_DATABASE_ID are required), keyed by database user, with an optional "*" default for every user not listed.

The identity of a session is the database user it authenticated as, so give each agent its own database user and a policy for that user. Under a policy, every reference counts (WHERE, JOIN, subqueries, RETURNING, not only what the query returns), DDL is always denied, and the identity cannot be changed from inside the session (SET ROLE, USE, COM_CHANGE_USER and the like are denied). A policy in observe mode records what it would deny and forwards the query.

The full behaviour (name resolution, writes and locks, policy changes on open sessions, telemetry, known limits) is in docs/AGENT_ACCESS.md.

配置

All variables are dialect-agnostic — the same names apply to every engine.

必需的

多变的 描述
UPSTREAM_HOST Hostname of the real database to proxy to

Ports

多变的 默认 描述
UPSTREAM_PORT protocol default¹ Port of the upstream database
PROXY_LISTEN_PORT protocol default¹ Port the proxy listens on

¹ Defaults follow VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL: Postgres 5432 upstream / 5433 listen; MySQL 3306 upstream / 3307 listen.

其他一切

The rest is optional and documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md:

  • Control-plane link (VERICTO_API_URL, VERICTO_API_KEY, VERICTO_DATABASE_ID, all three together): reports decisions to the Vericto API and syncs the workspace's rules and policy. Without it the proxy still protects with the built-in ruleset, and reports nothing. Also covers the telemetry buffer, over the monthly quota, disk spool size and several proxies on one volume.
  • TLS on each hop, client→proxy and proxy→database. On MySQL, TLS must be on both hops or neither.
  • Query size limit (VERICTO_MAX_QUERY_BYTES, 10 MiB by default).
  • Business policy rules (VERICTO_POLICY_RULES, off by default): a preview, off unless you turn it on; with it off the proxy behaves exactly as 4.14.3. With it on, the proxy applies only sync bundles whose Ed25519 signature verifies (VERICTO_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEYS for a control plane other than Vericto's).
  • Health check for load balancers (VERICTO_HEALTHZ_PORT).
  • Observability: logs, and metrics as Prometheus or CloudWatch EMF.
  • CPU sizing: capacity per vCPU, when to scale out (CPU at 50–60% of the task's reservation), and VERICTO_WORKER_THREADS (by default sized from the container's CPU limit, 1 worker on a 0.5 vCPU task).
  • Engine-specific notes, including MySQL details (TLS, protocol compression).

To run from source and run the tests, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

码头工人

Release images are published on Docker Hub as vericto/vericto-proxy (from 4.14.1 on) and at ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, and pull without credentials. The release workflow copies the multi-arch index it pushed to GHCR, so both registries serve the same digest under the same tags (<version>, <major>.<minor>, <major> and latest): pull from whichever your environment allows.

# Postgres. On Linux, add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway
docker run --rm -e UPSTREAM_HOST=host.docker.internal -p 5433:5433 \
  vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0

# MySQL
docker run --rm \
  -e VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL=mysql \
  -e UPSTREAM_HOST=host.docker.internal \
  -p 3307:3307 \
  vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0

# The same image from GHCR
docker pull ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0

Images released from now on carry a build provenance attestation (Sigstore, GitHub Actions) that ties their digest to this repository, the release workflow and the commit. Verify one before you deploy it, and deploy by digest:

gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:<version> --repo vericto/vericto-proxy

# Docker Hub (4.14.1 and later): the same digest, attested under its Docker Hub name
gh attestation verify oci://docker.io/vericto/vericto-proxy:<version> --repo vericto/vericto-proxy

Each platform image (4.15.2 and later) also carries a signed SPDX SBOM attestation, made for the platform manifest's digest (docker buildx imagetools inspect lists both):

gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/vericto/vericto-proxy@<platform digest> \
  --repo vericto/vericto-proxy --predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3

The runtime base is Chainguard glibc-dynamic (4.15.2 and later; debian:bookworm-slim before): glibc, libgcc and the CA bundle, no shell and no package manager. The proxy runs as 65532:65532 (nonroot; it was 1001:1001 up to 4.15.1, so chown a volume an older image wrote, or pass --user 1001:1001). Health checks call the binary instead of a shell, in exec form: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/vericto-proxy", "healthcheck"] (Docker Compose healthcheck.test, ECS healthCheck.command). It connects to the healthz listener (VERICTO_HEALTHZ_PORT) and exits 0 when that succeeds or the port is not set, 1 otherwise. A CMD-SHELL check, bash -c, curl or wget fails in this image.

To build the image from this checkout instead:

docker build -t vericto/proxy:local .

With Docker Compose:

proxy:
  image: ${VERICTO_PROXY_IMAGE:-vericto/vericto-proxy:4.17.0}
  ports:
    - "5433:5433"
  environment:
    UPSTREAM_HOST: postgres
    UPSTREAM_PORT: "5432"
    PROXY_LISTEN_PORT: "5433"
    # For MySQL: VERICTO_WIRE_PROTOCOL: "mysql" + the matching ports.
    # Optional — uncomment for telemetry + rule sync (all three together):
    # VERICTO_API_URL: "https://api.vericto.com"
    # VERICTO_API_KEY: "${VERICTO_API_KEY}"
    # VERICTO_DATABASE_ID: "${VERICTO_DATABASE_ID}"

Connection strings

Connection string
Postgres via proxy postgres://user:pass@localhost:5433/mydb
MySQL via proxy mysql://user:pass@localhost:3307/mydb

Same credentials as a direct connection — only the host/port change.
